What this count includes

Accounts in LiNEAR, Meta Pool, rNEAR and the recognized validator pools below. An account must have at least one matured balance above 0.01 NEAR; smaller amounts are excluded. Each account is counted once, including contract and lockup accounts that may need a different withdrawal route.

These are snapshot balances, not guaranteed payouts. The live checker verifies availability before offering a withdrawal. The total sums the listed balances. A protocol’s own balance can represent the same NEAR as its users’ balances, so adding both can count the same money twice. This isn’t a total of unique lost funds.

SMALL TOOL. CLEAR BOUNDARIES.

Made to be checked, not trusted.

Look first.

Scanning reads public chain data. No wallet, no signature, no sign-up.

Withdrawals go only to you.

FOUND asks your wallet for one withdraw call on the protocol’s own contract. That call pays the account that signs it, so there is no destination to change. No access key, no custody, no fee.

Check the work.

Every result names the block it was read at, and every withdrawal is confirmed against its public receipt. The read-only API is public. Source publication is planned for submission.

Checks LiNEAR, Meta Pool, rNEAR and indexed validator pools on NEAR mainnet. Pool discovery can miss recent activity. Aurora has read-only coverage. Other custom pools, tokens and bridges aren’t covered. A clear result only covers the places checked.

How recovery tracking works

FOUND records withdrawal requests and verifies their public transaction receipts. Totals count confirmed withdrawals and unique accounts. We don’t collect browsing analytics or wallet keys. Tracking may miss a withdrawal if the service is unavailable.
